Targeted re-review — sprint `2026-09-20-evidence-pipeline-integrity`, review_run_id 1baf009c-066a-46d9-a040-5b023d1b8fb3, mode: design. Read-only, no files written. Hashes re-verified on disk: design.md = d1d4cf4b…8171, review-packet.md = bd8a289d…2aca (both match dispatch); packet `source_design_sha256` matches design.md.

P1-1: CLOSED — design.md:35 states the rule token-wise ("A `|` is a pipe operator only as a standalone token: the `|` inside `||` and inside quotes is not"), and design.md:42 + AC2 put `npm test | tail -8 || echo done` explicitly in the non-admissible set; the real CC lexer does emit `||` as a distinct op (`vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.cjs:140-143`, verified: `npm test | tail -8 || echo done` → `npm test OP(|) tail -8 OP(||) echo done`).
P1-2: PARTIAL — `||`/`;` masking is now correctly non-admissible, but the `&` half is unimplementable under the design's own "pure move" constraint (`pre-bash-guard.cjs:118-147` never emits `&`: `npm test &` tokenizes to a single segment `[npm test &]`; `vibeCoding/codex/9.9.9/.codex/hooks/pre-bash-guard.py:176-188` likewise returns `[('npm test &', '')]`), so under a verbatim extraction `npm test &` lands in the final pipeline as its last segment → admissible → `pass`, the exact opposite of AC2.
P1-3: CLOSED — design.md:56 and the File Structure Plan design.md:74 now name `cc-core/_input-binding.cjs`, `cc-core/pre-bash-guard.cjs` and the new `cc-core/_shell-lex.cjs`; I re-verified byte-identity (`_input-binding.cjs` CC=PI=30a88e4bf884800b…, `pre-bash-guard.cjs` CC=PI=3a9ee518d015c883…), that Pi has no `evidence-collector.cjs`, and that nothing enumerates cc-core files (`athena-gates.ts:19,26` resolves by path; `pi-agent/plugin/package.json` lists only the two extensions), so a new sibling module is deployable as described.
P1-4: PARTIAL — the extract-instead-of-duplicate decision is right and the require chain is genuinely acyclic (`pre-bash-guard.cjs:357` → `_input-binding.cjs:5` → `_index-io.cjs`; CX `pre-bash-guard.py:350` function-local `from _input_binding import capture_before`, `_input_binding.py:14` → `_index_io`; a leaf `_shell-lex` added under both is a DAG, and CX bare-name imports resolve via sys.path[0]=script dir), and the CC tokenizer is a pure function with no guard state, so the CC move really is pure — but the design's premise is false on CX: `split_segments` (`pre-bash-guard.py:176-188`) is **not** quote-aware (verified: `go test -run 'A|B' ./...` → `[("go test -run 'A", '|'), ("B' ./...", '')]`, and `_input_binding.classify_validation("go test -run 'A")` → `"test"`), so extracting it verbatim makes CX downgrade the very command AC3 requires to stay admissible.
P1-5: CLOSED — AC4 now mandates a CC-shaped `{stdout, stderr, interrupted: false}` response with no `exit_code` plus a `PostToolUseFailure` leg; that event is really registered (`vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/settings.json:168`) and really consumed (`evidence-collector.cjs:44-55`), so the production branch at `:52-53` gets exercised instead of the existing `exit_code: 0` pattern.

[P1] design.md:27,35,39 + AC2/AC5 — "pure move, no tokenizer behavior changes" and the `&`/`|&` split rules are mutually exclusive, and the naive fix breaks AC1's own canonical command — Neither lexer emits `&` or `|&` today (`pre-bash-guard.cjs:140-143` pairs only `&&`/`||`, single-char ops only `;`/`|`; `pre-bash-guard.py:182-185` the same); adding `&` as an operator does change guard decisions, proven live: `echo hi & rm -rf /` is allowed today on both ends (CC exit 0, CX exit 0) while `echo hi; rm -rf /` blocks (exit 2, "recursive force removal of root/home"), so AC5's "no behavior change to guard decisions" and AC2's `npm test &` case cannot both hold. Worse, `&` is currently safe only because it is not an operator: `npm test 2>&1 | tail -8` tokenizes to `[npm test 2>&1] | [tail -8]`; naive `&` splitting yields `[npm test 2>] & [1] | [tail -8]`, putting the validation outside the final pipeline and turning AC1's copyable command non-admissible. The design must state the redirection-aware `&` rule (`&` not preceded by `>`/`<`, plus `|&`/`&>`/`>&`), and must own the guard-decision delta with a characterization test — no test pins the current segmenter behavior (no hits for `commandSegments`/`split_segments`/`npm test &` in `vibeCoding/scripts/tests/athena999/`).
[P1] design.md:36-40,42 + AC3 — the final-pipeline rule is wrong for `&&` and self-contradictory — Bash propagates the left operand's failure through `&&`, so `npm test && echo ok` cannot mask a failure, yet design.md:42 lists it as not admissible (a false downgrade that blocks ship on a correct command). Conversely rule 6 ("every classified validation segment must satisfy rule 3") kills the design's own admissible example: the live classifier returns `lint` for `npm run lint` (`vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/_input-binding.cjs:8-16`, verified `classifyValidation("npm run lint") === "lint"`; CX identical), so in `npm run lint && npm test` the `npm run lint` segment is a classified validation outside the final pipeline → non-provable, contradicting design.md:42 and AC3. Correct formulation: a segment is provable if every operator between it and end-of-line is `&&`, or it is in the final pipeline under pipefail/last position. Also unspecified: `classifyValidation` is whole-command and returns one kind, so "classified validation segment" needs a per-segment re-classification step the design never describes (CC tokens are quote-stripped, and `COMMAND_PREFIX` anchors on `^|[;&|]`).
[P1] design.md:25,27,62 (AC3) vs pre-bash-guard.py:176-188 — AC3's "CC and CX return identical verdicts and reasons for the whole matrix" is unreachable with the stated verbatim extraction — CX's splitter is quote-blind, so `go test -run 'A|B' ./...` → two segments with `classify_validation` matching the first fragment, giving `unknown`/`pipeline_without_pipefail` on CX against admissible/`pass` on CC; `pytest -k "a|b"` splits the same way. Making CX quote-aware is a real guard-decision change (it stops splitting quoted operator text that the guard currently inspects — the permissive direction, e.g. `echo 'x | rm -rf /'`), so the design must either budget that change with tests or drop the "no behavior change" claim; it cannot keep both AC3 and AC5.
[P2] design.md:64 (AC5) — "the Pi `cc-core` copies remain byte-identical to their CC originals" is unreachable under a directory-wide reading — `cc-core/delivery-gate.cjs` (PI 31bc03feacd6e00a… vs CC f872810e7c14d4fc…) and `cc-core/session-start.cjs` (PI 8c2664b2dd0f2caa… vs CC 9e03d35be7c833c6…) already diverge; scope the AC and the test to an explicit file list.
[P2] design.md:69-70,74 + athena-gates.ts:33-39,42-43 — splitting the guard into two files creates a new fail-open mode — a top-level require of `_shell-lex.cjs` that is missing in an installed/partial copy makes node exit 1; Pi maps any non-2 exit to "allow" (`blockDecision` at `athena-gates.ts:42-43`, spawn/timeout also returns code 0 at `:37-38`) and CC treats exit 1 as non-blocking, so the guard silently disappears. Note today's `_input-binding` require sits inside a try/catch (`pre-bash-guard.cjs:357`) precisely to avoid this; the design should state the placement and let slice 9 package-parity cover it.
[P2] design.md:52 + File Structure Plan design.md:73 — the CX 120 → 500 command-limit change ships with no AC and no test mandate — `evidence-collector.py:146` vs `evidence-collector.cjs:96`; no test asserts either bound today, and no AC1-AC6 clause covers the new value, so the change is unverifiable at review time. Either fold it into AC3 or drop it from this slice.
[P2] design.md:47 — the `result_reason` enum does not cover the cases the policy adds — only `pipeline_without_pipefail` and `validation_not_final_command` are defined, while backgrounding (rule 5) and `||`/`;` masking are semantically neither "pipeline" nor necessarily "not final"; since AC3 requires identical reasons on CC and CX, the enum must be pinned exhaustively before impl.
[P2] design.md:27 vs roadmap `.ai_state/roadmap/q12-batch2-production-gaps/roadmap.md:73,76` — the scope expansion removes slice 8's independence — roadmap row 8 records dependencies = none and line 76 allows slices 1-4/7/8 to proceed in parallel when write sets are disjoint; this slice now owns `pre-bash-guard.{cjs,py}` plus the new `_shell-lex` module on three platforms, so the write sets overlap and slice 8 must be sequenced after slice 2. The stated boundary is workable, but the design should record the new ordering constraint explicitly.
